draft.editorial_headline: INRAE book explains AI methods for linking food and bioproduct data to decisions
draft.editorial_deck: The volume describes ways to connect varied evidence and expert knowledge, with examples in packaging and cheese production.
draft.what_happened: INRAE describes a book coordinated by its scientists about knowledge engineering for food and bioproduct industries. It sets out methods for connecting experimental data, expert knowledge and stakeholder preferences so they can inform decisions.
draft.why_it_matters: The examples show where these methods could be applied, including packaging choices and cheese quality. The article describes the methods and applications, without reporting measured improvements from their use.
draft.for_humans: The book describes decision tools that bring different evidence and stakeholder preferences into view.
draft.for_ai: The methods formalize expert knowledge and connect varied data for automated reasoning.
body_paragraphs: Food and bioproduct research draws on chemistry, microbiology, nutrition and other fields. INRAE says the data can differ in format and completeness, so the methods first relate them through a shared vocabulary.

The book describes workflows to collect, organize and update information. Its examples include biodegradable packaging materials, food packaging choices and technological recommendations for cheese quality. It also discusses decisions involving several stakeholders whose preferences may conflict.
draft.limitation: This is INRAE's description of a book; the article does not provide measured outcomes for the described tools.

support.quote: Un nouvel ouvrage coordonné par trois scientifiques INRAE, Patrice Buche, Pierre Bisquert et Rallou Thomopoulos, présente les méthodes développées notamment à Montpellier pour transformer données et connaissances en outils d’aide à la décision.
L’ouvrage présente des chaînes de traitement – ou workflows – permettant de collecter, organiser, partager, relier et actualiser différentes sources d’information

Ces méthodes sont illustrées par des applications très concrètes dans les filières alimentaires et les bioproduits : conception de matériaux composites d’emballage biodégradables, choix d’emballages alimentaires ou encore formulation de recommandations technologiques pour améliorer la qualité des fromages.

draft.editorial_headline: Nanjing University begins AI literacy course for new students with a caution about hype
draft.editorial_deck: University leader Tan Tieniu opened the course with basic concepts, applications and limits of AI.
draft.what_happened: Nanjing University says Tan Tieniu gave the first lecture of its AI literacy core course to incoming undergraduate and graduate students. He covered AI concepts and applications, and urged students to assess inflated claims about what the technology can do.
draft.why_it_matters: The university plans AI teaching across undergraduate majors and makes general AI instruction part of incoming graduate students' required courses. This is an education plan and opening lecture, not evidence of learning outcomes.
draft.for_humans: New students are being taught AI concepts alongside its current limits and common misconceptions.
draft.for_ai: The university plans practical activities and cooperation with AI companies as part of the course.
body_paragraphs: Tan distinguished specialist, generative and embodied AI and discussed examples of their use. He warned students against treating broad claims, including claims that AI already has human feelings, as established facts.
The university says its course will include later sessions with specialists and practice activities. It reports the start of the program but gives no measure of what students have learned from it.
draft.limitation: The source is the university's report of its own opening lecture and plans; it does not report educational results.

draft.editorial_headline: Qingdao article maps local robotics and computing projects as an industrial AI bet
draft.editorial_deck: City reporting describes robot training facilities, industrial models and computing infrastructure while arguing for further investment.
draft.what_happened: A Qingdao city article surveys local efforts in physical AI, which connects software decisions with action in the physical world. It describes robot training facilities, factory AI projects and computing infrastructure, alongside the city's plans to expand those sectors.
draft.why_it_matters: The article shows how Qingdao is positioning its manufacturing and data assets for emerging AI markets. Its forecasts and ambitions are the city's claims, not measured future economic results.
draft.for_humans: The article describes local industrial projects, without establishing their effects on workers or residents.
draft.for_ai: Local companies are developing robot control and industrial models that link sensing, planning and action.
body_paragraphs: The report points to industrial models and robots being trained with real-world data. It says Qingdao is building training sites for embodied AI and describes factory systems under development by local companies.
It also lists computing centers and projects meant to supply AI services. The piece argues that these investments could strengthen the city's industry, but those future outcomes remain projections.
draft.limitation: This city-affiliated article combines reported projects with forecasts and advocacy; future effects have not been measured in the source.

draft.editorial_headline: Unitree says it is researching a self-improving model for physical AI robots
draft.editorial_deck: Chair Wang Xingxing described a proposed cycle of simulation, real-world testing and feedback at a company event.
draft.what_happened: Unitree says it is doing preliminary research on a model for physical AI robots. Its chair described a system that would search research papers, write code, train in simulation and test in real settings before feeding results into another round.
draft.why_it_matters: The plan shows how Unitree wants to automate parts of robot-model development. The source reports a research proposal, not results showing that the new model works.
draft.for_humans: The company described a future research process, not an observed change for robot users or workers.
draft.for_ai: If developed, the proposed system would use test feedback to guide further model training.
body_paragraphs: The announcement came at a Unitree partner event in Hangzhou focused on physical AI. Wang Xingxing described a loop in which an AI model gathers information, builds and tests in simulation, then checks performance in real environments.
The event also announced a physical AI competition. Unitree reported production and sales progress for an existing humanoid robot, which is separate from the preliminary model research.
draft.limitation: The self-improving model is in preliminary research; the report provides no performance result for it.

draft.editorial_headline: China's industry ministry describes its AI manufacturing push and planned product support
draft.editorial_deck: At a press briefing, an official described industrial AI programs and plans for devices and suppliers.
draft.what_happened: Ministry official Wei Wei said China is promoting AI in manufacturing. He cited work on industrial applications, datasets and device standards, then outlined plans to develop practical solutions and support AI-enabled products.
draft.why_it_matters: The remarks set out ministry priorities for AI in production and consumer devices. The progress figures are ministry claims, while the proposed steps are plans rather than measured future results.
draft.for_humans: The plans include wider availability of AI devices, but the source does not measure consumer effects.
draft.for_ai: The ministry plans to support industrial AI solutions and application service providers.
body_paragraphs: Wei described applications in manufacturing sectors and work to build industrial datasets and standards. His account also cited the ministry's estimates of industry size and adoption; those figures are official claims from the briefing.

Next steps include developing solutions for practical settings, renewing AI devices and linking product suppliers with buyers. The official mentioned computers, phones, robotics and medical equipment among the areas the ministry wants to support.
draft.limitation: This is an official account of programs, estimates and plans; the supplied transcript does not independently verify their effects.

draft.editorial_headline: Villefranche groups invite people to discuss AI uses and unanswered questions
draft.editorial_deck: A local information meeting lists everyday tools, misleading media, human roles and possible technical progress as topics.
draft.what_happened: A Villefranche-de-Rouergue notice announces an information meeting about what artificial intelligence is and how it works. It lists voice assistants, recommendations, translation tools and chatbots, alongside misleading videos and altered images.
draft.why_it_matters: The organizers invite people to discuss whether AI might influence decisions or replace human roles, and where it could bring technical progress. The notice poses these as questions; it reports no answers or observed effects.
draft.for_humans: The notice raises questions about AI shaping decisions and replacing human roles; it does not say those effects have occurred.
body_paragraphs: Guilhem Landès will lead the discussion. The notice says he has more than ten years of experience helping families and organizations address internet risks through training, content and awareness work.
The Association Familiale Laïque and Maison de l’amitié de Villefranche propose the meeting. The announcement gives discussion topics but no findings about specific AI systems.
draft.limitation: This is an event announcement. Its questions about AI are discussion topics, not findings.
